P1a.reply:
This matches the QSAR biodegradation data set from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. It has 1,055 chemicals, 41 molecular descriptors, and a binary label (ready biodegradable vs. not ready biodegradable). It was published by Mansouri et al. (2013), "Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship models for ready biodegradability of chemicals," in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling.


calls.reply:
I'm working from memory of the QSAR biodegradation column order, which I can't verify here, so these scores are rough estimates.

The columns, as I recall them: 0 SpMax_L, 1 J_Dz(e), 2 nHM, 3 F01[N-N], 4 F04[C-N], 5 NssssC, 6 nCb-, 7 C%, 8 nCp, 9 nO, 10 F03[C-N], 11 SdssC, 12 HyWi_B(m), 13 LOC, 14 SM6_L, 15 F03[C-O], 16 Me, 17 Mi, 18 nN-N, 19 nArNO2, 20 nCRX3, 21 SpPosA_B(p), 22 nCIR, 23 B01[C-Br], 24 B03[C-Cl], 25 N-073, 26 SpMax_A, 27 Psi_i_1d, 28 B04[C-Br], 29 SdO, 30 TI2_L, 31 nCrt, 32 C-026, 33 F02[C-N], 34 nHDon, 35 SpMax_B(m), 36 Psi_i_A, 37 nN, 38 SM6_B(m), 39 nArCOOR, 40 nX.

From the published QSAR biodegradation results and general experience with this data set, the features I expect to matter most are:
- SpMax_L (0)
- J_Dz(e) (1)
- SM6_L (14)
- F03[C-O] (15)
- Me (16)
- SpPosA_B(p) (21)
- SpMax_A (26)
- Psi_i_1d (27)
- SdO (29)
- TI2_L (30)
- SpMax_B(m) (35)
- SM6_B(m) (38)
- nHM (2)
- nO (9)
- HyWi_B(m) (12)
- C% (7)
- LOC (13)
- Mi (17)
- nCIR (22)
- F04[C-N] (4)
- B04[C-Br] (28)
- Psi_i_A (36)

The remaining features are mostly sparse count variables, so I scored them low.
